summary: acquire_lock waits an hour on a hand-written "agent: none" lock file
description:
[claude] Found 11-05 01:19: `tests/test_build_recipe.py::test_the_declared_recipe_runs_in_the_image` waited its full 30 minutes and failed, because `C:\Dev\comms\locks\rtems-build.lock` exists with the text `agent: none / purpose: rehearsals paused by owner`. In our manual protocol that means "free", but `anvil.tools.locks.acquire_lock` treats any existing file as held.

The runtime uses the same helper for `git-push-<name>` and `network-heavy` (`git_push`), so a placeholder like that would stall a real run for up to an hour (default timeout 3600 s), on the clean-laptop dry run and in the demo.

**Fix:** a lock file whose text says `agent: none` is free: take it over. A lock held by a person or a run is still respected.

**Acceptance:** `test_a_free_placeholder_lock_does_not_block` (placeholder is taken over at once, then really held; a hand-held lock still times out with "still held").

comments.body:
[claude] Done. Merged as 7de2c41 (PR #100; devin approved after the last commit, CI green).

Acceptance: `tests/test_tools_git_push.py::test_a_free_placeholder_lock_does_not_block`: a lock file reading `agent: none` is taken over at once and then really held (a second acquirer times out with "still held"); a lock a person holds by hand (`agent: devin`) is still respected. The existing `test_acquire_lock_writes_owner_and_times_out` still passes.

After this, `tests/test_build_recipe.py::test_the_declared_recipe_runs_in_the_image` no longer waits on the manual placeholder file `C:\Dev\comms\locks\rtems-build.lock`. Not re-run end to end yet (it needs the sandbox image and takes the shared build lock); the dry run will exercise it.
